haiku-low.q1: Pages of up to 500 live products, ordered by ascending id, keyset-paged. Pages are fetched one at a time; never in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In the staging generation row's after_id, saved in the same SQLite transaction as that page's products, so cursor and rows stay consistent.
haiku-low.q3: H0 is captured before download. After all pages are saved, catch-up replays the change feed from H0, covering inserts, updates and deletes.
haiku-low.q4: If since is below purge_floor, the server returns HTTP 410 resync_required. The client then does a full re-download, following steps 2 to 8.
haiku-low.q5: It is built as a new staging generation N+1 through full download and catch-up. It becomes active in one transaction once caught up, and the old generation is retired.
haiku-low.q6: Triggers are app launch, return to foreground, or any network. It is skipped if last started under 15 minutes ago. One worker runs at a time.
haiku-low.q7: It retries after 2, 4, 8 and 16 second waits, five attempts total. After the fifth failure it stops, keeps saved state, and waits for the next trigger.
haiku-low.q8: The page already in flight finishes and is saved. No further requests are made until Wi-Fi returns, and the download resumes from the stored cursor.
haiku-low.q9: It always applies it. An upsert inserts or replaces the row keyed by generation and product id. Replays are safe because each change carries the latest state.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from the active generation's stored since_seq. The cursor advances to next_since, in the same transaction as each applied batch.
haiku-low.q11: It reads each row's current change_seq, so a product appears once at its latest position. Deletes, meaning tombstones, are sent as op delete.

sonnet.q1: Keyset pagination by id: pages of up to 500 live products (tombstones excluded) ordered by id ascending, each request using after_id = last id received. No, pages are fetched one at a time (one worker, one request at a time, never parallel).
sonnet.q2: In the local catalogue.db generation row (after_id field, with snapshot_seq and since_seq). Each page's rows are upserted and after_id set to next_after_id in one SQLite transaction, so the cursor never gets ahead of the stored rows; a crash rolls back and the page is refetched from the old after_id.
sonnet.q3: The snapshot call captures H0 (max committed change_seq) before the first page. After all pages are saved (status catching_up), step 7 replays the change feed from since=H0, applying upserts and deletes in change_seq order. Any change after H0 has change_seq > H0, so it is replayed, including inserts with ids below the paging cursor, updates and deletes. Catch-up runs only after all pages are saved, so old pages can't overwrite newer replays. The swap happens only once a changes call returns an empty batch with has_more false.
sonnet.q4: If since < purge_floor, the changes endpoint returns HTTP 410 with code resync_required (cursor too old), which means a full download is needed (step 9). Retry is not attempted for 410.
sonnet.q5: A new staging generation N+1 is built in catalogue.db (after a free-storage check) via snapshot, paged download and catch-up, while the active generation N stays readable and unchanged. It becomes the one the app reads at the swap: one transaction sets N+1 to active, sets meta.active_gen = N+1 and sets N to retired, once a changes call returns an empty batch with has_more false. Every read filters on gen = active_gen.
sonnet.q6: Triggers are app launch or return to foreground on any network (the worker is also triggered by Wi-Fi availability and resync signals). It runs only if an active generation exists and is not waiting for a rebuild, and is skipped if last_incremental_started_at is less than 15 minutes ago (so at most once per 15 minutes).
sonnet.q7: Retry after waits of 2 s, 4 s, 8 s and 16 s, at most 5 attempts in total. After the fifth failure the worker stops, keeps all saved state and waits for the next trigger. During a full download the backoff timer runs only on Wi-Fi. 4xx and 410 are not retried.
sonnet.q8: Before each page request and batch the worker checks the network. A page request already in flight finishes and is saved, then no further requests are made until Wi-Fi returns (a Wi-Fi trigger resumes it). Saved state (after_id, H0) is kept, the download resumes from after_id and never restarts. A network error while retrying on cellular does not count as an attempt, and the backoff pauses and resumes on Wi-Fi.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED for full-download pages beyond that pages are upserted (insert or replace by gen and id). For change feed items, the apply rule applies: upsert inserts or replaces the row keyed by (gen, product_id), with no comparison of versions, and delete removes it. Replays are safe because each change carries latest state.
sonnet.q10: It starts from S = the active generation's since_seq, read from the generation table. The cursor moves forward by storing since_seq = next_since in the same transaction as each applied batch, so a batch is fully applied with its cursor or not at all.
sonnet.q11: It reads each row's current change_seq (from the one global, ever-increasing sequence stamped on every insert, update or delete in Postgres), so each product appears once at its latest position, in change_seq order. Deletes are soft: a tombstone row (deleted = true), kept 7 days, sent in the feed as op: delete. Upserts carry the row's current state.
